Lawnmowers (also called mowers or lawn-cutters) are heavy, often very noisy, lawn care vehicles for cutting grass. Most often, lawnmowers are used to cut grass on lawn turf.
Lawnmowers can have a wide range of types, from small, simple push mowers for small gardens to very large, heavy-duty models for cutting grass on sports fields and other large areas.
The most common types are lawn tractors, front-wheel lawn mowers, side-wheel lawn mowers and riding lawn mowers. They most often use gasoline engines to power the cutting mechanism. Electric or battery-powered mowers do also exist.
Many people, as well as cities and states, also restrict the noise level produced by lawnmowers.
The first mechanically controlled and automated lawn mower was designed by Nathaniel Baldwin of Philadelphia in 1830.
Lawnmowers can differ in several ways: the engine size and power, blade width and length, weight, type of cutting mechanism, cutting widths, and even whether it will run on gas, diesel, electricity, battery, or perhaps hybridization. A lawn mower might also have some other optional attachments, for grass-blending, edging, and other lawn-related tasks.
Lawn mowers are used in yards, parks, gardens, sports fields, and for various agricultural uses.
Lawnmowers are not used to cut wood, and should not be used to cut firewood, even if the wood is from a yard. The cutting mechanism typically cannot reach all the way through wood, and when used this way, it is likely to be damaged.
This should be obvious since a chainsaw can be used to cut firewood.
Even if a lawn mower cuttings are dry grass, they are not suitable as fuel for a fire. The grass is full of chemicals which would produce a strong, unpleasant smell and very high temperatures during burning that could cause harm to people, pets, livestock, and buildings.
It is a waste of money to bag and dispose of such grass clippings. There is so much energy in lawn waste that it could actually be used to produce compost, which is an excellent fertilizer, and a useful tool for creating healthier, happier lawns.
